AstraNova Biopharma - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AstraNova Biopharma Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss AstraNova Biopharma's financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Scientific Officer; Tom Reilly, Head of Commercial; Karen Lee, Head of Manufacturing; and David Kim, Head of Regulatory Affairs.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO of AstraNova Biopharma.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. AstraNova Biopharma delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust demand for our flagship oncology assets like NovaBlock and NovaMab, continued pipeline advancements, and operational efficiencies across our global footprint. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including enhancing gross margins through manufacturing optimizations, managing patent exposures with innovative lifecycle strategies, controlling operating expenses while investing in high-potential R&D, expanding geographically especially in emerging markets, strengthening our balance sheet and cash flows, securing key regulatory approvals and label expansions, and driving marketing effectiveness to boost sales uptake.

We're particularly excited about NovaLink, our bispecific T-cell engager, and its potential to capture meaningful share in solid tumors with projected peak sales exceeding $2 billion.

Now, I will turn the call over to Michael Chen, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Chen, CFO:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $1,400 million, an increase of 22% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by volume growth in NovaBlock and NovaMab, initial contributions from NovaLink, and strong emerging market expansion.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $350 million, or $1.25 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $420 million, or $1.50 per share.

Our operating expenses were $452 million, reflecting targeted investments in R&D for late-stage trials like BOLT-301 while maintaining SG&A discipline through headcount optimization and digital tools.

Let me expand on our gross margin performance and the manufacturing efficiencies driving it, which continue to be a cornerstone of our profitability profile here at AstraNova Biopharma. Our portfolio is heavily weighted toward high-complexity biologics—primarily our flagship monoclonal antibody NovaMab for oncology, alongside our recently launched bispecific T-cell engager NovaLink and our growing gene therapy platform. These assets demand precision manufacturing but deliver industry-leading margins when scaled effectively.

For the third quarter, we delivered a GAAP gross margin of 79.2%, up 420 basis points year-over-year from 75.0% and 110 basis points sequentially from Q2's 78.1%. On a non-GAAP basis, excluding certain one-time manufacturing variances from last year's tech transfer for NovaMab's process intensification, our gross margin expanded to 80.5%, marking the highest quarterly level in our history and surpassing our peers like Regeneron and Amgen, who reported blended margins around 77-78% in their recent quarters. This performance reflects a deliberate strategy to optimize our cost of goods sold, or COGS, which declined 8% year-over-year to $285 million, despite the revenue increase.

Product mix contributed approximately 250 basis points of expansion. NovaMab, our $2.5 billion annual revenue anchor, now represents 65% of total sales, up from 58% last year, with its mature margins north of 85% reflecting full scale-up at our primary U.S. facility in Devens, Massachusetts. Conversely, our earlier-stage gene therapies, like NovaGene-101 for rare diseases, carry launch-year margins around 60-65% due to per-patient fill-finish complexities and lower initial yields. As these ramp—with NovaGene-101 volumes doubling quarter-over-quarter—we expect mix to further favor high-margin biologics, targeting 82%+ non-GAAP gross margins by year-end.

Manufacturing efficiencies accounted for over half of our margin beat, delivering 200+ basis points of improvement. Our COGS per gram of drug substance for mAbs fell 12% year-over-year to $45 per gram, well below the industry benchmark of $55-60 cited in recent IQVIA reports. This stems from several technical initiatives across our global network: full transition of 80% of our mammalian cell culture lines from traditional fed-batch to intensified perfusion modes at our Devens and Limerick, Ireland sites, boosting bioreactor titers from 4.5 g/L to 6.8 g/L—a 51% yield improvement—while reducing cycle times by 25% from 14 to 10.5 days. Downstream purification enhancements, extending chromatography resin lifetimes from 50 to 100 cycles via proprietary cleaning-in-place protocols validated under FDA process performance qualification, cut resin costs by 18%, with process analytical technology using real-time Raman spectroscopy slashing defect rates from 2.5% to 0.8%. Global capacity utilization hit 87%, up from 72% a year ago, with our new 50,000L Singapore facility running at 75% capacity and serving APAC markets with 20% lower labor and energy costs through partnerships like WuXi Biologics.

U.S. operations drove 60% of the efficiency gains, benefiting from Inflation Reduction Act incentives, while Europe faced slight headwinds from EMA single-use system validations. In Asia, Singapore mitigated biosimilar erosion on legacy products. Long-term contracts with Lonza and Cytiva locked in 85% of raw materials through 2025, shielding from 10-12% inflation, and NovaMab royalties remain flat at 8%.

Looking forward, we guide to Q4 non-GAAP gross margins of 81-82%, with full-year 2024 at 79.5-80%, assuming NovaMab demand growth in a 12% expanding oncology market. We're committing $450 million in CapEx next year for gene therapy lines, partnering with Samsung Biologics, targeting 300+ bps annual expansion through 2026.

Turning to operating expenses for the quarter, which provide context on managing our cost base amid pipeline advancement and commercialization scaling for NovaCure, our BTK degrader for CLL. Total operating expenses came in at $452 million, up 16% year-over-year from $390 million, and 8% sequentially from Q1. As a percentage of trailing twelve-month revenue of $4.8 billion—driven by immunology like NovaRelief—OPEX was 37.7%, up 200 bps YOY, in line with peers during pipeline phases.

R&D was $325 million, 72% of OPEX, up 22% YOY, driven by clinical acceleration in BOLT-2 for BOLT-301 bispecific in gastric cancer ($120 million), technical initiatives for mRNA platform ($85 million) with AI from Insilico, and early discovery in CRISPR-Cas13 ($65 million). Excluding $15 million milestones, core R&D grew 18%, on track for $1.25-1.35 billion full-year.

SG&A was $127 million, up 4% YOY, with $70 million for NovaCure commercial ramp and $57 million G&A efficiencies from Salesforce AI and legal for patent litigations. We're prioritizing zero-based budgeting for 5-7% savings, pipeline focus saving $40 million, and Asia shifts.

Now, our geographic revenue breakdown underscores our balanced footprint. Total net product revenues were $1,400 million, up 22% YoY. North America: $784 million, 56%, up 12% on NovaBlock NSCLC and biosimilars. Europe: $336 million, 24%, up 11% CER on tender wins. Rest of World: $280 million, 20%, up 32% CER, with emerging markets at $168 million, up 42% YoY—China $92 million up 52% on NRDL inclusion for NovaBlock biosimilar, Asia ex-China $37 million up 35%, Latin America $25 million up 30%, others $14 million up 25%. We're investing $300 million in EM R&D and biosimilars for 35-40% growth.

Cash flow and balance sheet remain strong: $2.8 billion cash, up 18% sequentially; net debt $4.2 billion at 1.8x EBITDA. Operating cash flow $925 million, up 32%, from $1.6 billion revenues including NovaBlock $850 million. Investing outflow $650 million on R&D capex and M&A; financing $200 million on buybacks. FCF $450 million, guiding FY24 $2.3-2.5 billion.

Before guidance, key assumptions for FY2025 revenue growth of 18-22% to $4.2-4.5 billion, with NovaBlock at 60%, assuming 65-70% PTS for BioGeneX gene therapy, milestones from CRISPR, 4-6% U.S. ASP erosion offset by EU/China growth. Risks include clinical binary outcomes, competition from Regeneron/Roche, IRA pricing, supply disruptions, macro rates, IP litigations.

On patent cliff: 28% of revenues ($4.1 billion) at risk 2026-2028 from NovaBlock ($2.9B), Lipara XT ($900M), Nexovar ($300M), with U.S. 62% exposure. Mitigated by $1.2B LCM investments: label expansions like NovaBlock TNBC/NSCLC adding $500M, formulations, combos with BNT-402 launch 2026, IPRs staving generics.

For full year, updating guidance to revenue $5.2-5.4 billion, EPS $6.00-6.50.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Lisa Patel, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Michael. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, enrollment in BioGeneX Phase 3 is 95% complete, with topline Q4 2025; BOLT-301 advancing; NovaCure MCL expansion captured 28% share. We expect multiple readouts in H2 2025.

Next, Dr. Raj Singh will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. We are making significant strides in early-stage research, including AI-accelerated discovery via ExaMol reducing timelines 40%, CRISPR-Cas13 for rare diseases, mRNA optimizations, and 15 novel targets identified. Our LNP platform shows 2x transduction efficiency.

Now I'll turn the call over to Tom Reilly, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Tom Reilly, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Raj. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with prescriptions for Zepara-like NovaBlock growing 28% QoQ to 1.47 million TRx, NRx 42% YoY. Market share 14.2% in T2D/oncology segments. Sales force productivity at 12.4 HCP touches/week, 17.2% conversion, CAC $4,200, LTV:CAC 34:1. Marketing spend $287 million yielded 5.2x ROI, with DTC 4.2x, digital 24% conversion, KOL endorsements up 31% NRx. U.S. 87% revenues, Europe 3.1% share, China 65% TRx growth. Omnichannel AI boosts close rates 11%, targeting 20% NRx acceleration.

Next, Karen Lee will discuss our manufacturing operations.

Karen Lee, Head of Manufacturing:
Thank you, Tom. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly. Capacity utilization 87%, perfusion yields up 51%, resin costs down 18%, Singapore facility at 75%. No disruptions, dual-sourcing mitigations, focused on CapEx for viral vectors and overflow with Samsung.

Finally, David Kim will provide an update on regulatory submissions and approvals.

David Kim, Head of Regulatory Affairs:
Thank you, Karen. We continue to work closely with agencies. Achieved FDA full approval for NovaCure MCL expansion (68% ORR), GBX-278 adolescent psoriasis (82% PASI 90), GBX-519 SMA to 18 years (92% milestones), GBX-742 RMAT for gastric. EMA/PMDA/Japan follows, NMPA filings. These add $1.8B peak sales, de-risk $15B pipeline.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Elena.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thank you, David. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the patent cliff, can you elaborate on LCM offsets for NovaBlock?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thanks, John. Michael, want to take that?

Michael Chen, CFO:
Sure. We've invested $1.2 billion in label expansions like TNBC adding $500 million, formulations, combos, and IPRs on 70% litigations, projecting 65-75% offset through 2030 with pipeline like BNT-402.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen, Morgan Stanley:
Great, thanks. Thoughts on gross margin risks from IRA?

Michael Chen, CFO:
Margins are resilient at 80.5% non-GAAP, with innovative pipeline outside near-term clawbacks. Pricing reforms modeled at 3-5% ASP hit, offset by volume and efficiencies.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee, JPMorgan:
On clinical risks for BioGeneX?

Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer:
Thanks. 65-70% PTS based on LNP advantages, immunogenicity monitored below 30%, 9-12 month FDA review assumed, with PRIME fast-track.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim, Barclays:
Marketing ROI details for emerging markets?

Tom Reilly, Head of Commercial:
EM CAC half U.S. at $2,800, digital-first driving 65% China TRx growth, NRDL leverage, targeting 15% total share.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the AstraNova Biopharma Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
